findings.title: annual_split crashes with KeyError('F1_2') on real fold tags — any non-vacuous scored run is guaranteed to abort; §8 'annual split correctness' test absent
findings.detail: evaluate.annual_split line 75 does out[r['fold'][:4]] += r['net_pnl'] for F1/F2 rows, but 'F1_2019'[:4] == 'F1_2' (and 'F2_2020'[:4] == 'F2_0') while out's keys are '2019'/'2020'/'2021'/'2022'. Reproduced directly against the committed module: KeyError 'F1_2' on the first F1 row. run_cells scored mode calls annual_split unconditionally (line 108) AND via concentration (line 134) AND drop_one (line 152) — every cell, so the scored run cannot complete once any F1 row exists (always true for a non-vacuous book). Fail-closed (crash, no wrong numbers emitted) but it is a guaranteed mid-run abort with §5 observed-denominator ambiguity — the exact blocking class as r1 H-4, now by outright bug instead of absence. Root enablement: plan §8 mandates an 'annual split correctness' golden test; none exists, which is why 19/19 passed while the scored path is broken. (Repair is A1's prerogative; not specified here.)

findings.title: matched_book_folds: fold_summary raises on any fold-flat matched book — conditional scored-run crash
findings.detail: run_cells builds rec['matched_book_folds'] = {f: EV.fold_summary(mb_rows, f) for f in E.FOLDS}; fold_summary raises FailLoud when a fold has zero rows. If the matched book is flat in any fold (fewer than 10 picks on every date of that fold — plausible under the >=10-picks rule), the scored run aborts mid-way. Fail-closed direction, but same §5 trial-accounting ambiguity class as H-6/M-2. Benchmarks are evaluation context; a flat fold should be reportable as flat, not fatal (behavioral note, not a repair instruction).

verdict_rationale: Round-2 remediation is substantively good: all five r1 HIGHs were addressed pre-PnL with plan A4 + family_contract v2 + impl_contract v2 pins, the SPY benchmark is now the frozen buy-and-hold, the matched book is live and non-vacuous, the evaluation layer exists in full, and the fresh 31.9s dry-run re-scans clean by my own recursive scan. But the H-4 fix introduced evaluate.annual_split with a fold-tag slicing bug ('F1_2019'[:4] == 'F1_2') that I reproduced directly against the committed module; scored mode calls it unconditionally three times over, so the first scored cell is guaranteed to abort — and the §8 'annual split correctness' golden test that would have caught it does not exist (hence 19/19 green over a broken scored path). One unresolved HIGH forces REFUSED under the unchanged zero-HIGH rule; a mid-scored-run crash also creates the §5 observed-denominator ambiguity flagged in r1. The asymmetry is acknowledged: this is likely a one-line slice defect plus one missing golden test, but repair is A1's prerogative and re-audit is mine.
